specs.title: Customer — Modernization Specification
specs.description: Extract the Customer bounded context (owner pages + owners table) into an independent service.
specs.context: The Owner page navigates to GET /owners/{id}, which reads the owners table. The UI, API, and data layers are currently co-deployed in the monolith.
specs.business_narrative: The Customer capability is the clinic's front door: front-desk staff register pet owners and look up their contact details and pets. Modernizing it into an independent service lets the clinic evolve owner management without redeploying the whole monolith.
kpis: A front-desk clerk can register a new owner in under two minutes.
Owner lookups return in under one second for 95% of requests.
business_glossary: Owner: a pet's registered guardian and the clinic's primary point of contact.
Pet: an animal registered under an owner and seen by the clinic.
assumptions: Front-desk staff access the system from an authenticated clinic workstation.
Owner records are migrated with their full pet and visit history.
business_risks: Losing owner history during migration would break visit lookups and erode staff trust.
Slow owner lookups at the front desk would create check-in queues.

requirements.statement: The Customer service exposes GET /owners/{id} returning an owner aggregate.
requirements.constraint: Response must include first_name, last_name, and pets list.
requirements.rationale: The Owner page is the primary read path for the Customer context.

requirements.statement: The owners table is owned exclusively by the Customer service; no other context writes to it.
requirements.constraint: No direct cross-service SQL writes; all mutations go through the Customer service API.
requirements.rationale: Database ownership is the strangler-fig extraction boundary.

acceptance_criteria.given: A valid owner id exists in the owners table
acceptance_criteria.then: The response is 200 with the owner aggregate including first_name, last_name, and pets list

acceptance_criteria.given: An owner id that does not exist
acceptance_criteria.then: The response is 404 with a structured error body

acceptance_criteria.given: Another service attempts a direct SQL write to the owners table
acceptance_criteria.then: The write is rejected by the database role grant; only the Customer service role has INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on owners

test_scenarios.scenario: GET /owners/{id} returns owner aggregate for a known id
test_scenarios.preconditions: Owner with id=1 exists in the test DB

test_scenarios.scenario: GET /owners/{id} returns 404 for an unknown id
test_scenarios.preconditions: No owner with id=9999 in the test DB

test_scenarios.scenario: Direct SQL INSERT to owners table from a non-Customer role is rejected
test_scenarios.input: INSERT INTO owners (first_name, last_name) VALUES ('X', 'Y') executed as vet_service_role
test_scenarios.expected: PostgreSQL error: permission denied for table owners

architecture_decisions.title: Front the owners table with a Customer repository port
architecture_decisions.context: The owners table must be exclusively owned by the Customer service to enable extraction.
architecture_decisions.decision: All reads and writes to the owners table go through a CustomerRepository port in the Customer service; no other service may use a direct DB connection to owners.
consequences: The storage engine can change without touching callers.
A migration shim is needed during the strangler-fig transition.
alternatives: Shared DB schema — rejected: blocks independent deployment.
Event sourcing — deferred: too high complexity for this context.

user_flows.name: View Owner Detail
steps: User navigates to the Owner List page
User clicks on an owner's name link
System renders the Owner Detail page with the aggregate
user_flows.sequence_diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as OwnerDetailComponent
  participant API as OwnersController
  participant SVC as OwnerService
  participant DB as owners
  UI->>API: GET /api/owners/{ownerId}
  API->>SVC: getOwner(ownerId)
  SVC->>DB: SELECT * FROM owners WHERE id = ?
  DB-->>SVC: owner row + pets
  SVC-->>API: OwnerResponse
  API-->>UI: 200 OwnerResponse

nfrs.requirement: GET /owners/{id} must respond in < 200ms at p95 under 50 concurrent users.

dod_extra: The owners table has no inbound foreign keys from other bounded contexts.

adrs.title: Adopt strangler-fig extraction sequencing
adrs.context: The monolith has cross-layer UI to API to DB threads that must be extracted without a big-bang cutover.
adrs.decision: Extract bounded contexts in dependency-wave order (leaves first), routing traffic through a facade during the transition.
consequences: Each wave is independently deployable and reversible.
A facade/routing layer must be maintained until the last context is extracted.
alternatives: Big-bang rewrite — rejected: unacceptable cutover risk.
Freeze-and-fork — rejected: diverges the two codebases.
